THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM)
The captioned appeal is by the claimants who have questioned the compensation determined by the Tribunal in MVC.No.398/2012.
The respondent No.2/Insurance company admits its liability and therefore, the appeal is purely on quantum.
The claimants who are mother and siblings of deceased Vijaykumar have filed a claim petition claiming compensation.
The said Vijaykumar died in a road traffic accident on 09.05.2012.
A claim petition was filed contending that deceased was a driver by profession and was getting a salary of Rs.12,000/- p.m.
The claimants to substantiate that deceased was a driver and was employed, relied on salary certificate vide Ex.P-14.
Though Tribunal accepted the claimants contention that deceased was working as a driver, however, declined to accept the contention of the claimants that deceased was earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
In absence of income proof, the Tribunal assessed the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.7,000/- and proceeded to award compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' at Rs.7,56,000/-.
Feeling aggrieved by the quantum determined under the head of loss of dependency, the claimants who are the mother and siblings have filed this captioned appeal.

sentences.text: 3. Heard learned counsel appearing for the claimants and learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2/Insurance company.
4. On reassessing the evidence on record, this Court is inclined to accept the notional assessment of income assessed by the Tribunal.
This Court, however, has noticed that Tribunal has not added future prospects and therefore, warrants interference at the hands of this Court.
If the income of the deceased is assessed notionally at Rs.7,000/- and 40% is added towards future prospects, the income is taken at Rs.9,800/-.

Deceased was admittedly was a bachelor and therefore, after deducting 50% towards personal expenses, the income is assessed at Rs.4,900/- and by applying the multiplier of 18, the compensation re-determined under the head 'loss of dependency' works out to Rs.10,58,400/- (4,900x12x18).
5. Under conventional heads, a sum of Rs.70,000/- is awarded.

The accident is of the year 2012 NC:
2024:KHC-K:8538 and therefore, in the light of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.1, 10% escalation for every three years which works out to Rs.14,000/- is added.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The total compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.11,42,400/- as against Rs.8,06,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

6. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed-in-part;
